summary: Action plugins look like modules in playbooks and always run on the control node; some do all the work (debug, assert), most prepare data then invoke a module, like template building a file locally then calling copy; normal runs modules without special action plugins.
questions: Does the debug task run on the managed node?
How does the template module actually work under the hood?
What is the normal action plugin?
Where is the documentation for an action plugin kept?

answer_card.title: How action plugins relate to modules
answer_card.answer_md:
Action plugins appear as modules to playbook authors; docs usually live in a same-named module. They **always run on the control node**.
- Some do everything locally: `debug`, `assert`.
- Most prepare values locally and then run a module remotely, e.g. `template` renders a temp file locally, transfers it, then runs `copy` on the target.
- `normal` runs modules with no special action plugin.
